items_missed: No usable greeting — the opener was garbled to the point the customer asked 'can you hear me / who are you' three times and never learned who was calling or from what company
Never asked 'How are you today?' and never used the customer's name (Tiffany) a single time in a 10-minute call
No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation — the call jumped straight into detail collection
No 'pricing is super simple' framing; the hourly rate ($105/mover) only came out after the customer asked for it twice, and after the total had already been quoted
Never listed what's included in the rate (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands, tools)
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned — no insurance explanation at all, on a move with two mattresses, TVs and 20+ boxes going into storage
'No hidden fees' pitch never delivered — and the wardrobe-box charge was explained so poorly the customer said 'I'm so confused', plus two different prices were quoted ($14 then $18)
Entire Clock section missed: no 'clock starts on-site', no prorated 15-minute increments, no sense-check — and the minimum was stated WRONG as 'two hours' instead of 2.5 hours
Estimate delivered as a bare number ('six hours, $1,260') with no typical time range for this size job and no explanation of how it was built
Mover count and truck size were only given because the customer asked; stairs at the two-story origin and assembly/disassembly time were never raised as time variables despite both applying
No Save Your Ass prep speech — prep came up only reactively ('depends on how well prepared you are'), with no consolidation examples and no 'take a carload' tip
No BOLDED-details framing for the confirmation email, no 'reply with any corrections'
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' — the customer ended the call herself
Business hours / how to reach us never given
Customer said 'sorry, stressful day' at the close and it went completely unacknowledged
top_strength: Roselyn ran a genuinely thorough intake on the storage destination — she probed the unit's floor, indoor vs. outdoor, climate control, and dimensions, and correctly explained WHY climate control matters (walk distance from where the truck can park). That is the one place on the call where she connected a question to a real cost driver.
coaching_note: The single biggest fix is the opening 60 seconds. This call started with a garbled, unidentified greeting — the customer asked 'who are you?' and 'is this Joanna?' and Roselyn spent the next minute spelling her own last name instead of confirming she was speaking with Tiffany about her Aug 30 move. That opener cost her the customer's confidence for the whole call, which is why Tiffany drove every remaining topic (hourly rate, truck size, payment method, mover contact) instead of Roselyn. Drill the scripted open: clear company + name ID, confirm the customer's name and use it, 'how are you today?', recap the move on file, then the agenda statement and 'sound good?'. Second fix, same call: the Clock section was skipped entirely and the minimum was misquoted as two hours instead of 2.5 — that is a factual error that will surface on the invoice.
phone_presence_notes: Largely mechanical and reactive — zero use of the customer's name, no affirmations or empathy markers, repeated dead air ('give me one sec') and a confusing fee explanation that left the customer saying 'I'm so confused', with her closing 'stressful day' comment ignored.
audio_review_reason: Phone presence scored 2, and the transcript shows a possible line/audio quality problem at the open ('can you hear me', 'I'm getting every of barely') — worth verifying whether the flat read is delivery or a bad connection before coaching on tone.
